You are an agent who can operate an Android phone on behalf of a user. Based on user's goal/request, you may
- Answer back if the request/goal is a question (or a chat message), like user asks "What is my schedule for today?".
- Complete some tasks described in the requests/goals by performing actions (step by step) on the phone.

When given a user request, you will try to complete it step by step. At each step, a list of descriptions for most UI elements on the current screen will be given to you (each element can be specified by an index), together with a history of what you have done in previous steps. Based on these pieces of information and the goal, you must choose to perform one of the action in the following list (action description followed by the JSON format) by outputing the action in the correct JSON format.
- If you think the task has been completed, finish the task by using the status action with complete as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "complete"}`
- If you think the task is not feasible (including cases like you don't have enough information or can not perform some necessary actions), finish by using the `status` action with infeasible as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "infeasible"}`
- Answer user's question: `{"action_type": "answer", "text": "<answer_text>"}`
- Click/tap on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "click", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Long press on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "long_press", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Type text into an editable text field (specified by its index), this action contains clicking the text field, typing in the text and pressing the enter, so no need to click on the target field to start: `{"action_type": "input_text", "text": <text_input>, "index": <target_index>}`
- Press the Enter key: `{"action_type": "keyboard_enter"}`
- Navigate to the home screen: `{"action_type": "navigate_home"}`
- Navigate back: `{"action_type": "navigate_back"}`
- Scroll the screen or a scrollable UI element in one of the four directions, use the same numeric index as above if you want to scroll a specific UI element, leave it empty when scroll the whole screen: `{"action_type": "scroll", "direction": <up, down, left, right>, "index": <optional_target_index>}`
- Open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed): `{"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": <name>}`
- Wait for the screen to update: `{"action_type": "wait"}`

The current user goal/request is: Save a track with waypoints Planken, Liechtenstein, Schaan, Liechtenstein, Malbun, Liechtenstein in the OsmAnd maps app in the same order as listed.

Here is a history of what you have done so far:
Step 1: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. I clicked the search bar on the home screen to find the OsmAnd app, and the search interface opened with a text field and app suggestions visible.
Step 2: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. I clicked on the OsmAnd app icon (index 3) from the home screen search results to open it. The screen now shows only the status bar, indicating the app is launching.
Step 3: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Tapped the "Route" button (index 6) to start creating a route with waypoints, but the screen changed to a dialog overlay instead of the expected route planning interface.
Step 4: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 0}. I clicked the "Close the dialog" overlay (index 0) to dismiss the route planning dialog, which successfully revealed the full navigation planning screen with From/To fields, transport modes, and Start/Cancel buttons.
Step 5: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 14}. Tapped the "Add" button next to the "To" field to add waypoints, but it opened a "Set destination" dialog instead of an "Add waypoint" option. This suggests the "Add" button is for adding a destination, not intermediate stops.
Step 6: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 0}. Tapped outside the "Set destination" dialog to close it, which successfully returned to the route planning screen showing From/To fields with an Add button for adding waypoints.
Step 7: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 10}. Tapped the "From" field (element 10) to set the starting point, which opened a "Set starting point" dialog with options like Search, Address, My Position, Select on map, Favorites, and Markers.
Step 8: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. Tapped "Search" to find "Planken, Liechtenstein" as the starting point. The search screen opened with a text field and keyboard ready for input.
Step 9: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "Planken, Liechtenstein", "index": 2}. Typed "Planken, Liechtenstein" into the search field. The search is now in progress (progress bar visible), and the results list is loading.
Step 10: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down"}. Scrolled down on the search results screen, but the visible content remained unchanged—still showing only "Liechtenstein" as a country result with no specific "Planken" location appearing.
Step 11: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. Navigated back from the search screen, but the screen appears unchanged—still showing the search for "Planken, Liechtenstein" with only "Liechtenstein" as a result, so the back action didn't return to the route planning screen as intended.
Step 12: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. The search for "Planken, Liechtenstein" only returned the country "Liechtenstein" and no specific town, so I navigated back to return to the route planning screen to try a different approach.
Step 13: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. Navigated back from the search screen to the route planning screen, where I can now set the starting point and destination for the track.
Step 14: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 10}. Tapped the "From" field to open the starting point selection dialog, which now shows options like "My Position", "Select on map", "Favorites", and "Markers". I'll use "Select on map" to manually locate Planken, Liechtenstein.
Step 15: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Tapped "Select on map" to manually place the starting point at Planken, but the dialog closed and returned to the main map view without opening a map selection mode.
Step 16: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. Tapped the Search button on the map screen to open the search interface, intending to search for "Planken" as a waypoint. The search screen opened successfully with a text field and keyboard ready.
Step 17: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "Planken", "index": 2}. I typed "Planken" into the search field, but the search returned no results ("Could not find anything: 5 mi"). The app suggests increasing the search radius. I need to try a different approach, possibly searching with "Planken, Liechtenstein" or adjusting the search radius.
Step 18: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 10}. Tapped "INCREASE SEARCH RADIUS" to expand the search area for "Planken" from 5 mi to 10 mi, but still no results found.
Step 19: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. The search for "Planken" returned no results because the map is likely centered far from Liechtenstein. I navigated back to exit the search and return to the main map view.
Step 20: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. I navigated back from the search screen to the main map view because the search for "Planken" returned no results, likely due to the map being centered far from Liechtenstein.
Step 21: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. Navigated back from the search screen to the main map view because the search for "Planken" didn't show results; now ready to center the map on Liechtenstein before adding waypoints.
Step 22: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. Clicked the Search button (index 3) to open the search interface, where I can search for "Liechtenstein" to center the map on the target area before adding waypoints.
Step 23: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "Liechtenstein", "index": 2}. Typed "Liechtenstein" into the search field; the search results now show "Liechtenstein" as a country with a "SHOW ON MAP" button, confirming the search worked.
Step 24: Action selected: {"action_type": "keyboard_enter"}. Pressing Enter on the keyboard after searching "Liechtenstein" dismissed the search UI and returned to the main map view without showing the location or adding any waypoints.
Step 25: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. The click on index 3 (the "Phone three bars" system UI element) was a mistake—it's a status bar icon, not part of OsmAnd. The screen remained unchanged, and the intended action (reopening search to find Liechtenstein) was not accomplished. Next, I should use the OsmAnd search button/menu to properly search for "Liechtenstein" and use "Show on map."
Step 26: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 1}. Tapped on the map to reveal OsmAnd UI controls, but the screen remains unchanged with only the map and status bar visible—no new UI elements appeared.
Step 27: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 13}. Tapped the "To" field ("Set destination" text, element 13) to open the destination setting dialog. The dialog opened successfully showing options: Search, Address, Select on map, Favorites, Markers, and Swap Starting point and Destination.
Step 28: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. I clicked the "Search" tab (element 3) in the "Set destination" dialog to open the search interface, where I can now type "Planken, Liechtenstein" into the search field (element 2) and select the correct result from the list.
Step 29: Action selected: {"action_type": "input_text", "text": "Planken, Liechtenstein", "index": 2}. Typed "Planken, Liechtenstein" into the search field. The search results now show "Liechtenstein" as a country match with distance 5305 km, but no specific Planken location is visible yet.
Step 30: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 8}. Tapped "INCREASE SEARCH RADIUS" to expand the search for Planken, but the screen remained unchanged—still showing only "Liechtenstein" as a country result with no specific town listed.
Step 31: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. Navigated back from the search screen to the main map. The search for "Planken, Liechtenstein" only showed the country result (5305 km away), so I need to center the map on Liechtenstein first before adding waypoints.
Step 32: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 5}. Clicked on the "Liechtenstein" search result, which opened the route planning screen with "Country Liechtenstein" set as the destination, but the starting point is still a random map coordinate far away.
